facts.title: NASA — 1958 establishment
facts.text: The National Aeronautics and Space Act created NASA in 1958, and NASA began operations on October 1, 1958.

facts.title: Independence Hall — historic context
facts.text: Independence Hall in Philadelphia is historically associated with the United States’ founding documents; this source reference is retained with historic scope.

facts.title: Monroe Doctrine — 1823 historical record
facts.text: The Monroe Doctrine was articulated in President James Monroe’s annual message to Congress on December 2, 1823.

facts.title: Truman Doctrine — 1947 historical record
facts.text: On March 12, 1947, President Harry S. Truman presented the address known as the Truman Doctrine, seeking assistance for Greece and Turkey.

facts.title: Electoral College — electors and majority
facts.text: The United States Electoral College consists of 538 electors, and a majority of 270 electoral votes is required to elect the president.

facts.title: Declaration of Independence — July 4, 1776
facts.text: The Declaration of Independence is dated July 4, 1776.

facts.title: Alaska Purchase — 1867
facts.text: The United States purchased Alaska from Russia in 1867; Alaska was formally transferred to the United States on October 18, 1867.

facts.title: Louisiana Purchase — 1803
facts.text: The United States purchased the Louisiana territory from France in 1803.

facts.title: United States Constitution — 1787
facts.text: The United States Constitution was drafted during the summer of 1787 and signed on September 17, 1787.

facts.title: U.S. presidential term — four years
facts.text: Article II of the United States Constitution provides a four-year term for the president.

facts.title: Abraham Lincoln — sixteenth president
facts.text: Abraham Lincoln was the sixteenth president of the United States.

facts.title: Gettysburg Address — historic scope
facts.text: Abraham Lincoln delivered the Gettysburg Address at Gettysburg, Pennsylvania, on November 19, 1863; National Park Service historical material describes it as approximately two minutes long.

notes.title: Reference-place boundary
notes.text: Only neutral landmark and agency records are retained. Security-sensitive facilities and organization-characterization claims are withheld.

notes.title: Civil-rights and doctrine boundary
notes.text: Civil-rights and foreign-policy source material is retained only as historically bounded, externally supported context; compressed ideological claims are withheld.

notes.title: Printed-MCQ gate
notes.text: The source includes a printed answer grid, but no MCQ is imported until its full question, four options, key, label, and safe premise are individually reconciled.

notes.title: Constitutional-history boundary
notes.text: Historic constitutional records are retained with primary-source citations. Political, territorial, and premise-ambiguous source questions remain withheld.

notes.title: Source-error boundary
notes.text: The source’s 1863 slavery-abolition key is excluded: the National Archives distinguishes the limited 1863 Emancipation Proclamation from the Thirteenth Amendment’s 1865 abolition record.
